entries.note: Each launch creates a private unique configuration directory so concurrent agents cannot overwrite one another’s overlays. User/project files are never rewritten. OpenCode runtime JSONC and Gemini defaults are parsed and preserved; malformed input or a name collision fails visibly. Gemini uses the lowest-precedence defaults layer, so managed policy remains authoritative. Codex requires the injected MCP server to initialize; no permission-bypass flags are supplied. The claude branch also names the session: a minted identity is started with --session-id <agentId>, a bound one with --resume, and a launch whose own args already name a session is passed through untouched, because the identity IS that session id (spec 095, Identity).

Read the launch's own flags rather than inferring the conversation afterwards from a transcript, a process tree or a hook — an earlier attempt did that and kept getting it wrong. --session-id/--resume/-r with a valid UUID name the session, so it becomes the agentId and the args are left alone; -c/--continue, --resume with a search term instead of an id, and --fork-session all mint the id inside the CLI where rEngine cannot see it, so the identity is rEngine's own and records known:false rather than guessing. Values are lowercased because the ledger's header check is lowercase hex.
